new: The developer notebook (developer mode only): in a headset hold B or Y to record a spoken note, let go to send it. Each trigger press while recording drops a numbered pin where you point, and what was there is noted.

A note also keeps two pictures (as it began and as it ended, with the pins), and what the app knew then: the story or studio scene, the circle, how the headset lines up, the settings, the frame rate and the last log lines.
On a phone or laptop with developer mode on: a round microphone button at the bottom right. Press to record, tap or click anywhere to pin, press again to send.

Notes go to the relay. Its notes page, <relay>/notes/, plays them back, shows the pictures and pins, marks them done, copies one as text and deletes them. Claude reads and transcribes them from there.
No relay to hand: a note waits on the device and goes once one answers.
The menu's Circles tab has Back to the lobby: your story ends there and every circle shows again (not at the room's arc of cards).
test: Turn developer mode on. In VR or AR hold B for a moment: does the red read-out show? Say something, press the trigger at two things, let go. Does Note sent come?
Open stories.lab.lbi-netmed.com/notes/ on a laptop: is your note there, does it play, are the pictures and pins right?
If the microphone is refused in the headset, record one note from the 2D page first (the round button), allow the microphone, then try again in VR.
Record a quick note from your phone and from the laptop.
Press B or Y twice quickly: the frame rate still toggles, and a hold does not.
In a room with circles, at a story's circle: Circles tab, Back to the lobby.
untested: Everything on a real Quest: the microphone inside a session, the picture read from the headset's view, holding B or Y, pins on real things, the read-out.
In AR the picture shows only what the app draws (no passthrough). An iPhone's recording format and the notes page on a phone.
Back to the lobby on a headset.
